title: Interleaved traffic-weaving scheduler with lifecycle checkpoints
author: Anika Rao
description:
Background: Our current rollout controllers support phased canaries and traffic mirroring but treat cohort progression as monolithic ramps. This PR introduces a new scheduling strategy — TrafficWeaver — that interleaves short time-slices of traffic across cohorts so we can run interleaved A/B experiments and fast canaries together while preserving per-cohort lifecycle checkpoints (warmup, shadow-validate, ramp, steady, rollback-hold). Motivation: teams building latency-sensitive features need the ability to evaluate new model variants in parallel without long single-cohort drains, and to guarantee deterministic rollback windows tied to observable checkpoints. This reduces time-to-signal for regressions and improves safety when mixing short canaries and long A/B cohorts.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds a new scheduler component (trafficweaver.svc) that allocates traffic in millisecond time-slices and manages per-cohort state machines.
- Introduces lifecycle checkpoints for each cohort: warmup, kv-preload, shadow-validate, phased-ramp, steady, and rollback-hold. Checkpoints are pluggable and backed by metric predicates (latency, error-rate, quality-regressions).
- Implements latency-aware fallback: if the 95th latency of a cohort exceeds SLO threshold during warmup or ramp, the scheduler reduces weave percentage and eventually falls back to the control variant for pending requests.
- Adds deterministic cohort assignment with a configurable seed to ensure reproducible split behavior across restarts.
- Adds observability: per-cohort histograms (p50/p95/p99), rollout-phase gauges, weave-cycle counters, and a top-level rollout-traffic-heatmap metric for the console.
- Adds end-to-end tests for the weaving pattern and a synthetic integration test that exercises rollback based on a simulated quality regression.

Files/areas touched (high-level):
- services/trafficweaver/ — new service: scheduler, coordinator, checkpoint engine (core implementation).
- runtime/router/traffic_slice.go — new time-slice allocation logic and fallback hooks.
- api/rollouts/v1/plan.proto — extended RolloutPlan with weave configuration and checkpoint predicates.
- console/src/components/rollout/WeaveVisualizer.tsx — visualization for interleaved traffic and phase timelines.
- docs/rollouts/weaving.md — usage guide and examples.
- test/e2e/rollouts/weaver_integration_test.go — integration test harness + synthetic metric injection.

Commit summary (high-level):
- feat(trafficweaver): initial scheduler skeleton and weave loop (commit a1f2c3)
- feat(api): RolloutPlan weave config and checkpoint proto changes (commit b2d3e4)
- perf(router): optimized time-slice allocator and KV cache warmpath (commit c3e4f5)
- feat(console): Weave visualizer and new metrics panel (commit d4f5g6)
- test: e2e harness, unit tests for checkpoint evaluation (commit e5g6h7)
- fix: deterministic seed and stable hashing for cohort assignment (commit f6h7i8)
- ci: flaky test backoff and stable timing adjustments (commit g7i8j9)

Review conversation (high level and representative excerpts):
- Marco Alvarez (reviewer): "Nice approach. Two asks: 1) please ensure cohort assignment is deterministic across controller restarts; 2) can we expose a 'max-weave-window' to limit latencies for tail-sensitive apps?"
- Author (Anika Rao): "Implemented deterministic seed + stable hashing; added max_weave_window to weave config with default 200ms. Updated docs to call out latency trade-offs."
- Lina Zhou (reviewer): "The metrics look useful but we need per-model quality delta as an input to checkpoint predicates — can we plug into existing eval streams?"
- Author: "Wired an optional eval_stream endpoint and added a conversion layer in the checkpoint engine. If eval_stream is not provided, the checkpoint can consume user-provided sample sets."
- Greg Thompson (SRE): "CI initially failed on weaver_integration_test due to timing flakiness. After the backoff and increasing synthetic sample window the test stabilizes. Approving after green build."

CI summary:
- Initial pipeline: build passed, unit tests 98% green, e2e flaky (weaver_integration_test) failing intermittently due to timing in the harness.
- Action: added exponential backoff in the harness and moved the synthetic injection to the test-controlled clock.
- Final CI status: pass (all checks green on rerun).

Backward compatibility and safety:
- RolloutPlan extensions are additive; older controllers ignore weave fields. Default behavior remains existing ramping for plans without weave config.
- Default weave config is conservative (small slice size and short warmups) to avoid surprise impact.
- Checkpoint predicates are pluggable and default to SLO checks; operators can disable auto-rollback for manual rollouts.

Migration notes:
- No forced migration required. Teams who want weaving must opt into the new RolloutPlan.weave config.
- Console visualization appears only if the controller advertises weave support.

Merge outcome: merged via squash-and-merge after CI green and approvals from Marco Alvarez and Lina Zhou. Release notes included below.

Related work and tickets: ENG-9876 (traffic-weaver design), PM-411 (rollout UX for interleaved experiments), INT-403 (customer request for short canaries + A/B).
release_notes:
- Added TrafficWeaver scheduler for interleaved canary + A/B experiments.
- New RolloutPlan.weave config with lifecycle checkpoints and latency-aware fallbacks.
- Console visualization for interleaved traffic and rollout phases.
- New metrics: rollout.weave.cohort_latency_{p50|p95|p99}, rollout.weave_cycle_count, rollout.phase_gauge.
